_comment: Trailhead-only entries for foot trails whose polylines we could not pull from USGS (Layer 37 has gaps) or OSM Overpass (504 Gateway Timeout on 2026-04-19). Trailhead lat/lon are the published parking-lot coordinates from the managing agency (DNR, NPS, county). Users see a pin + data; no polyline renders.

trails.name: Maryland Heights Trail
trails.description: The classic Harpers Ferry viewpoint hike — a strenuous climb up the Maryland side of the Potomac to the Overlook Cliff, with a panoramic view of the confluence of the Potomac and Shenandoah. Rocky, steep, worth every step.
highlights: Panoramic view of three states from Overlook
trails.parkingNotes: Park at the C&O Canal Sandy Hook lot off US-340 and walk across the Goodloe Byron Pedestrian Bridge, OR park in Harpers Ferry and walk across the railroad bridge. No parking directly at the trailhead on the MD side.

trails.name: Annapolis Rocks (AT Spur)
trails.description: The most popular overnight destination on Maryland's section of the Appalachian Trail. A 2.5-mile climb from US-40 to a quartzite cliff overlook facing west over Greenbrier and the Cumberland Valley.
highlights: Black Rock Cliffs (0.8 mi further north)
trails.parkingNotes: US-40 AT crossing trailhead parking. Fills by 10 AM on fall weekends. Overflow parking on the shoulder is not recommended.

trails.name: Weverton Cliffs (AT Spur)
trails.description: Short but steep climb from the C&O Canal Towpath up to the southernmost overlook on Maryland's Appalachian Trail. Dramatic view up the Potomac water gap.
trails.parkingNotes: Weverton Road AT parking lot off US-340. Very small lot (12 spaces); alternative: park at Knoxville or walk from the C&O Brunswick lot.

trails.name: Calvert Cliffs — Red Trail
trails.description: The Chesapeake Bay cliff beach hike. 1.8 miles one way through forest and wetland to the fossil-rich cliff beach — world-class shark-tooth hunting at low tide.
highlights: Calvert Cliffs beach (Miocene fossil shark teeth)
trails.parkingNotes: Service fee per vehicle. Parking lot can fill on summer weekends by 11 AM.

trails.name: King and Queen Seat Trail
trails.description: Short steep scramble to the dramatic quartzite outcrop of the King and Queen Seat — one of the most photographed overlooks in Maryland.
highlights: King and Queen Seat rock outcrop
trails.parkingNotes: Hills Grove parking lot off MD-24. Service fee per vehicle.

trails.name: Kilgore Falls Trail
trails.description: Short walk to the 17-foot Kilgore Falls, Maryland's second-tallest free-falling waterfall. Popular swimming hole in summer.
highlights: Used in The Lord of the Rings (Sharkey's End scene)
trails.parkingNotes: Falling Branch entrance has timed-entry reservations required on peak summer weekends (May 15 – Oct 15). Reserve via park site.

trails.name: Choate Mine Trail — Soldiers Delight
trails.description: Loop through one of the rarest ecosystems in the East — serpentine barrens, home to grassland and pitch pine endemic to this 1,900-acre reserve.
trails.parkingNotes: Overlook Drive parking lot. Free. Visitor center open weekends.

trails.name: Seneca Creek Greenway Trail
trails.description: 16.5-mile stream-valley footpath from Rockville to the Potomac at Riley's Lock, following Seneca Creek through mixed hardwood forest.
trails.parkingNotes: Multiple trailheads — most common are Schaeffer Farms, Clopper Lake, and Riley's Lock (C&O MP 22). Riley's Lock lot fills by 10 AM.

trails.name: Hereford Gunpowder North Trail
trails.park: Gunpowder Falls State Park — Hereford Area
trails.description: Popular trout-stream footpath along the Big Gunpowder Falls in the Hereford Area. Catch-and-release fly fishing is top-tier here.
trails.parkingNotes: Masemore Road lot is the classic access. Free, but limited parking — alternate at Falls Road.

trails.name: Mason-Dixon Trail (MD Segment)
trails.description: Rugged bluff-top footpath along the Susquehanna River, part of the 199-mile Mason-Dixon Trail from Whiskey Springs (PA) to Chadds Ford (PA).
trails.parkingNotes: Rock Run Mill / Stafford Road lots. Conowingo Dam overlook has separate Exelon parking.

trails.name: Life of the Dunes Trail
trails.description: Short loop through the dune ecosystem with interpretive signage. Wild ponies frequently visible.
trails.parkingNotes: Assateague Island NS entrance fee or park pass. Parking at North Beach lot.

trails.name: Life of the Marsh Trail
trails.description: Short boardwalk loop through salt marsh with interpretive signage. Bird-watching hotspot.
trails.parkingNotes: Assateague Island NS entrance fee or park pass. Marsh trailhead parking lot.

trails.name: Sugarloaf Mountain Loop (Blue Trail)
trails.description: The full Sugarloaf circuit — 5.5-mile blue-blazed loop around and over the summit of Sugarloaf Mountain, with four overlook viewpoints. Privately owned but open to the public.
trails.parkingNotes: East View Parking (lower) or West View Parking (upper). Free, donations accepted. Gate closes 1 hour before sunset.

trails.name: Cat Rock (Catoctin)
trails.description: Less-crowded alternative to Hog Rock — quartzite outcrop with excellent views west across the Monocacy Valley.
trails.parkingNotes: Park at the Owens Creek picnic area lot or Visitor Center. Free.

trails.name: Chimney Rock & Wolf Rock Loop
trails.description: Classic Catoctin loop combining two of the park's signature rock outcrops — Chimney Rock and Wolf Rock — in a single strenuous circuit.
trails.parkingNotes: Visitor Center parking. Free; NPS park pass not required for day use.
